in_greek.name: Μπεκκα
in_greek.meaning: Παράγωγο του ονόματος Rebecca, που σημαίνει δέσποινα του σπιτιού
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μπεκκα είναι παράγωγο του ονόματος Rebecca, το οποίο προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή λέξη 'ריבקה' (Rivka) και σημαίνει δέσποινα του σπιτιού ή γυναίκα με πλούσιο σπίτι. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Ρεβέκκα συνδέεται με την Πατριάρχη του βιβλίου της Γένεσης.

data.cultural_impact: Becca is a name steeped in European history, particularly Germanic and Scottish heritage. Named after a fabricated Old High German word 'berhta', meaning 'bright or shining'. This moniker has a rich association with the nobility and brilliance, often adopted as a baby name to honor the beauty and potential of a newborn. In Anglo-Saxon England, it was a popular given name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Rebecca is the name of a significant matriarch in the Old Testament. Daughter of Bethuel and Rebekah, Rebecca was a tenant of faith and obedience. According to Biblical stories, God appeared to Isaac in a vision while he was meditating at Rehoboth in the Negev. Isaac asked the Lord for a wife from his own people, and God directed him to Rebecca. As she was on her way to meet Isaac, Rebecca showed signs of faith and piety, making sure to cover her face when she found out that she was going to marry her cousin Isaac, despite the cultural and moral taboo of cousin marriages at that time. Rebecca bore two sons, Jacob and Esau, through whom various biblical narratives were shaped. She was a devoted wife and a loving mother, embodying the virtues of faith, obedience, love, faithfulness, and compassion. In this capacity, the name Becca bears strong spiritual significance, reminding those who carry it of the importance of having faith, following God's will, and upholding love and loyalty in their relationships.
